criteria.name: Introduction — Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design; discusses the context of ethical issues in engineering organisations; identifies relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Several ethical issues and their significance identified, described, in the context of engineering design, understanding of BOTH context in engineering organisations and stakeholder interest is demonstrated.

levels.label: Very good
levels.desc: Several ethical issues identified, described, and linked to engineering design, understanding of context in engineering organisations OR stakeholder interest is demonstrated.

levels.label: Good
levels.desc: Few ethical issues identified, described, and linked to engineering design, but understanding of context and stakeholders is limited.

levels.label: Satisfactory
levels.desc: Few ethical issues identified and described, but the context and stakeholders are not identified.

levels.label: None
levels.desc: No ethical issues identified.

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions on the ethical issues; draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Objective arguments are made with significant depth, leading to conclusions on decision making recommendations for several different stakeholders.

levels.label: Very good
levels.desc: Objective arguments are made with appropriate depth. Conclusions are made on decision making, though lack of consideration of different stakeholders.

levels.label: Good
levels.desc: Arguments are made, though they lack depth or are based on personal opinion. Conclusions are made on decision making, though lack of consideration of different stakeholders.

levels.label: Satisfactory
levels.desc: Ideas are presented, though they lack the depth required to build arguments. Conclusion is made with no apparent link to the arguments.

levels.label: None
levels.desc: No arguments presented. No conclusions drawn.

criteria.name: Compelling Argument that supports conclusion — The report forms a compelling argument that justifies the conclusion; the body follows a logical structure, with linked paragraphs and content ordered to support the argument; arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Arguments are compelling, supported by the report structure. The conclusion is well supported by the arguments. The arguments demonstrate a systematic understanding of the ethical issues for all stakeholders.

levels.label: Very good
levels.desc: Arguments are compelling, supported by the report structure. The arguments support the conclusion, demonstrating a sound understanding of ethical issues.

levels.label: Good
levels.desc: Arguments are logically structured, though are not compelling. Conclusion is not well supported by the arguments presented.

levels.label: Satisfactory
levels.desc: Arguments are difficult to follow. Link to conclusion is unclear.

levels.label: None
levels.desc: Arguments are not evident. No conclusions drawn.

criteria.name: Research and Evidence — Arguments are substantiated with adequate references and qualitative/quantitative evidence; research demonstrates a balanced, in-depth understanding of the topic.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Arguments are well substantiated with references as well as both qualitative and quantitative evidence. Evidence of research demonstrates a balanced and in-depth understanding of the topic and its ethical issues.

levels.label: Very good
levels.desc: Arguments are substantiated with adequate references and some qualitative/quantitative evidence. Research demonstrates a good understanding of the topic.

levels.label: Good
levels.desc: Arguments are substantiated with some relevant references and qualitative OR quantitative evidence. Research demonstrates a moderate understanding of the topic.

levels.label: Satisfactory
levels.desc: Limited references that lack relevance to arguments, showing limited evidence of research.

levels.label: None
levels.desc: No references, or other evidence of research to support arguments.

criteria.name: Report Structure, Format and Language — The report includes appropriate sections serving their functions (abstract, introduction, body, and conclusion); maps, figures, tables, and visual elements are correctly used to support discussion; writing is grammatically correct, fluent, concise, easy to read and understand, and uses appropriate word choice; references are well-structured and appropriate, supporting the report’s motivations.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: The report is fluently written, has no incorrect uses of language, uses several types of visual elements competently, and uses relevant references extensively.

levels.label: Very good
levels.desc: The report is fluently written, has no incorrect uses of language, uses several types of visual elements competently, and uses relevant references.

levels.label: Good
levels.desc: The report is fluently written, has no incorrect uses of language, uses limited visual elements, and a few relevant references.

levels.label: Satisfactory
levels.desc: The report is fluently written, has few incorrect uses of language, very limited visual elements, and few, mostly irrelevant references.

levels.label: None
levels.desc: The report has incorrect uses of language, has no visual elements, expression is not fluent, and references are missing.
